quote: 6月30日,中文大模型评测机构SuperClue首次发布“Token成本象限图”,该象限维度由任务平均得分和平均每题价格来定义。结果显示,不同大模型的平均每题价格相差近20倍,任务平均得分最高相差超70%。
locator: paragraph 大模型决胜性价比
claim: Translation: On 30 June SuperCLUE first released a 'Token cost quadrant' defined by average task score and average price per question; per-question price differs ~20x and top score gap exceeds 70%.

quote: 其中,智谱GLM5.2(max)在任务得分和平均每题价格均为最高,领衔“高端质优”象限。小米集团的MiMo-V2.5-pro则以最低的平均每题价格和不俗的任务得分,领衔“经济适用者”象限。
claim: Translation: Zhipu GLM5.2 (max) is highest on both score and price, leading the 'premium quality' quadrant; Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5-pro has lowest price and decent score, leading the 'economical' quadrant. Model naming includes effort tag '(max)'.

quote: 还有其他大模型分布在“超值领航者”和“溢价探索者”象限。
claim: Translation: other models fall in the 'value pilots' and 'premium explorers' quadrants. Four quadrant names recorded.

quote: SuperClue本次测评了国内7个代表性大语言模型,测试任务是完成相同的工程问题,其间需驱动模型开展数十轮对话交互,逐步完成代码分析、修改与验证,最终得出不同模型的性价比、推理耗时、交互轮数和词元消耗数量。
claim: Translation: 7 domestic models; same engineering problem needing dozens of dialogue turns (code analysis, modification, verification); outputs value-for-money, reasoning time, turns and token consumption. Method: one agentic task, measured spend, not list price alone.

quote: 目前大模型变成了生产力工具,在关注模型效果的基础上,大众也关心调用词元的消耗情况以及最终完成任务的成本。
claim: Translation: models are now productivity tools; beyond quality, people care about token consumption and final task cost. Stated motive for the cost quadrant.

quote: 近日,多份中文大模型评测报告中首次新增成本评测,让用户得以通过定价看清开支。
locator: paragraph 1 大模型决胜性价比
claim: Translation: several Chinese LLM evaluation reports recently added cost evaluation for the first time. Indicates trend, not only SuperCLUE.

quote: 词元消耗如何折算成业务产出,目前尚无标准。由于AI供应商多元化,账单天然存在碎片化问题,没有一张表能看清全貌。
claim: Translation: there is no standard for converting token consumption to business output; billing is fragmented. Market-context statement by iResearch.

quote: Claude跑一轮测试的成本超200元,而DeepSeek仅花费17.1元,其余大模型开支则在数十元到百余元不等,相差悬殊。
claim: Translation: one round cost over 200 yuan on Claude vs 17.1 yuan on DeepSeek. Anecdotal user test, one task.

quote: 本次测评覆盖21款国内外主流模型,测评集包括六大任务:数学推理、科学推理、代码生成、智能体(任务规划)、精确指令遵循、幻觉控制,共492题。
claim: Translation: May 2026 SuperCLUE ranking covers 21 models, six tasks, 492 questions. This is the quality-only report; no cost dimension in the retrieved text. Distinct from the 30 June quadrant.

quote: OpenCompass is a one-stop platform for large model evaluation. It supports a wide range of models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, and more, and integrates over 100 datasets covering knowledge, reasoning, coding, science, language, long context, safety
claim: README describes capability dimensions only (knowledge, reasoning, coding, safety, etc.); cost or price is not among listed dimensions. Negative finding is for the README, not the live CompassRank page.

quote: The platform supports zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, rule-based, and LLM-as-judge evaluation, while task partitioning, concurrent execution, and distributed execution accommodate evaluation workloads
claim: Method features documented; no price-normalised ranking feature mentioned.

quote: the inference cost for a system performing at the level of GPT-3.5 dropped over 280-fold between November 2022 and October 2024. At the hardware level, costs have declined by 30% annually, while energy efficiency has improved by 40% each year.
claim: Stanford AI Index 2025 reports a >280x fall in inference cost at fixed GPT-3.5-level capability; it is a trend statement, not a model-by-model value ranking.

quote: AI agents already match human expertise in select tasks, such as writing Triton kernels, while delivering results faster and at lower costs.
claim: AI Index notes lower cost of agents on select RE-Bench tasks; qualitative cost note only.

quote: We propose measuring AI performance in terms of the length of tasks AI agents can complete. We show that this metric has been consistently exponentially increasing over the past 6 years, with a doubling time of around 7 months.
claim: METR headline metric is task length (time horizon); the retrieved text gives no cost or token-spend column. Negative finding limited to this post, not later METR reports.

quote: we use the token counts reported by each model's API provider where available, to accurately report the cost of running the Intelligence Index. In the rare cases where provider token counts are unavailable, we use a canonical-tokenizer fallback.
claim: AA computes Index run cost from provider-reported token counts (which include billed reasoning tokens where providers report them; inference, not stated explicitly in this sentence).

quote: When reporting cache hit rates and cost, we combine these token counts with live measurements of the model's typical cache hit rate, rather than relying on the one-off measurement when the evaluation was run.
claim: Cost uses live cache-hit measurements, so AA cost is not a pure list-price calculation.

quote: Reasoning models: Maximum output tokens allowed, as disclosed by model creators (custom setting for each reasoning model)
claim: Reasoning models run with their maximum output budget, which drives reasoning-token spend in the cost-to-run figure.

quote: This chart shows the average pay-per-token API cost per task across the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, spanning DeepSWE v1.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0, and SWE-Atlas-QnA.
locator: Cost per Task, What Cost Is Measuring
claim: AA agent cost is average API cost per task over three benchmarks.

quote: It is intended to show pay-per-token API cost, not consumer plan pricing or the full operational cost of deploying the system in production.
claim: AA explicitly excludes subscription-plan pricing, a contrast with ValueRank's plan-cost basis.

quote: Token usage matters because it often drives cost and can also indicate how much context an agent consumes to get work done, but token efficiency and cost are not identical because providers price token categories differently
claim: AA separates token efficiency from cost.

quote: Cost per successful task can diverge from token price by more than an order of magnitude, and it inverts the ranking the pricing pages give you.
claim: Vendor study (10 models, 40 tasks, 2,400 runs) argues cost per successful task beats token price.

quote: Coverage and cost are different questions: the cost-effective model reliably solved 8 of 40 tasks, the frontier tier 25 to 26. Report both.
claim: Arize reports coverage and cost separately, akin to quality vs cost split.
